primitives.name: Achievement Game GEN
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first player who builds a generating set from the jointly selected elements wins the achievement game denoted by GEN.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G': 'finite group, dimensionless', 'S': 'set of selected elements, dimensionless', 'nim(GEN(S))': 'nim-number of position S, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Players alternate selecting unselected elements; first to form a generating set wins.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S generates G, the game terminates with WIN for the last player.

layer2.mapping: GEN is isomorphic to a positional nim-game where nim(GEN(S)) = ∗nim(S) under Sprague-Grundy theorem.
layer2.telemetry: Terminal nim-number of game position determines win/loss.

primitives.name: Avoidance Game DNG
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first player who cannot select an element without building a generating set loses the avoidance game denoted by DNG.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G': 'finite group, dimensionless', 'S': 'set of selected elements, dimensionless', 'nim(DNG(S))': 'nim-number of position S, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Players avoid creating generating sets; game ends when no valid move remains.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When no element can be added without generating G, the current player loses.

layer2.mapping: DNG's nim-number kernel derived from automorphism equivalence classes of game digraphs.
layer2.telemetry: Nim-number of terminal position indicates loss condition.

primitives.name: Structure Diagram
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our main computational and theoretical tool is the structure diagram of a game, which is a type of identification digraph of the game digraph that is compatible with the nim-numbers of the positions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'SD(G)': 'structure diagram of game G, graph object', 'nim(SD(G))': 'nim-number assignment on SD(G), dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Game positions are identified up to automorphism equivalence; nim-numbers preserved.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When automorphisms collapse distinct positions, simplification occurs.

layer2.mapping: Structure diagram maps game digraph to quotient space preserving nim-numbers via automorphism orbits.
layer2.telemetry: Visual representation of nim-number consistency across equivalent game states.

reasoning_traces.think:
The achievement game GEN models a race to generate a group, where nim-numbers encode winning strategies. The avoidance game DNG models a race to avoid generating the group, with nim-numbers indicating losing positions. Both games are impartial, meaning their outcomes depend only on the current state and not on whose turn it is. The Sprague–Grundy theorem allows us to assign nim-numbers to each game position such that the overall game value equals the XOR of its component positions. Structure diagrams simplify this by collapsing symmetric game states, enabling efficient computation of nim-numbers. These primitives enable formal reasoning about game dynamics and strategic behavior in finite group settings.
